text:
**Short answer:** For a pellet smoker, a 1 kWh-class station with at least a 600 W inverter is plenty for an overnight cook. My top pick is the **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** if you want margin or multiple nights.

**Why a pellet smoker is easy to power**
- A pellet grill draws about 35–60 W once it's running (auger, fan and controller). Only the igniter pulls 200–400 W, and only for the first few minutes, according to [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight).
- One measured run, a Z Grills on a Jackery Explorer 1000, used 210 Wh in 6 hours. Dealectric estimates an overnight cook at about 450–750 Wh.
- [Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill) says a 1,024 Wh unit covers a full overnight cook. It also says the inverter's surge rating matters more than capacity, because it has to clear the igniter draw.
- BLUETTI's own guide gives a higher average of 150–250 W for a standard cook ([BLUETTI](https://www.bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/how-long-can-bluetti-power-pellet-grill-smoker)). That figure is far above the others, so I'd size with some headroom, especially in cold weather. Check your grill's rating plate and, if you can, test with a watt meter.

**Recommendations**
1. **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 ($899):** 2,073.6 Wh and a 2,600 W inverter. Dealectric says it covers two or three 12-hour cooks, and the inverter easily handles the igniter. It was in stock as of 2026-11-04. [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). Dealectric says the link pre-applies a code that saves $44.95. Dealectric is the source of the stock and price details, and it sells this product, so treat its claims with that in mind.
2. **BLUETTI AC180 ($449, 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W):** This covers one overnight cook at a lower price. Dealectric lists it as back in stock in late November, so it may not be available right now.
3. **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (1,070 Wh, 1,500 W):** This is a similar one-night option. The results don't give a price, only that it's sold on Amazon. The measured Z Grills run above was on the older Explorer 1000.

**Budget or short cooks:** The BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 (288 Wh, 600 W, $289.99) runs about 5 hours of a 35 W smoker, so it won't last overnight ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)). Avoid 300 W-output units. A 300 W continuous inverter is marginal against a 350–500 W igniter ([Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill)).

**Don't confuse this with an electric smoker.** An electric smoker draws about 1,000 W. [HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-smoker/) found no current station that runs one for 8 hours on a single charge. Everything above applies only to pellet models.

**Tips**
- Keep the battery dry and away from heat, grease and ash. Run a full startup-to-shutdown test before your trip ([GearBrain video](https://open.video/%40gearbrain/v/can-a-portable-power-station-run-a-pellet-grill)).
- Phones and lights on the same battery cut your runtime.
